newsitem.title: MEXICO: Rebels receive message of peace from Mexican leader.
newsitem.headline: Rebels receive message of peace from Mexican leader.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1996-12-08

text.p: Zapatista rebels in southern Chiapas state on Sunday received a message of peace from Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo, who also asked the rebels for 15 days to consider proposed changes to the consitution on Indian rights.

A legislative commission known as Cocopa delivered the rare missive by Zedillo to the rebels as lawmakers and rebels finished weeks-long talks aimed at amending the constitution to guarantee greater rights for millions of Mexican Indians.

"Cocopa delivered a message...in which the federal government reiterated its commitment to negotiate a peace accord with justice and dignity," Cocopa, a group acting as an intermediary between both sides, said in a statement.

Zedillo asked the rebels for up to 15 days to consider a proposal by both the Zapatistas and Cocopa that changes in the constitution be made to ensure an accord on Indian rights signed by both sides earlier this year be carried out.
Marcos said the peace process was in crisis on Friday, after the government made some "observations" on the proposed Indian rights bill this week that the rebels interpreted as a demand for changes.
The Zapatistas are not officially in talks with the government, but an agreement on Indian rights is considered a key step in restarting the stalled negotiations.
